narrative.overview:
Chelabase is drawn as a nautical chart of a lagoon at dusk. The main database is the fairway; branches are surveyed channels cut off it at tide marks. Every surface is chart material: a deep lagoon-teal ground, pastel depth fields that own whole regions, fine engraved linework, dashed survey lines, graduated neat-line borders, italic soundings and water names, and a title cartouche. Controls are chart furniture (cartouche plates, neat-line tabs, a tide staff), never stock component-library parts.

The system ships today on the landing app (`apps/landing`, `src/components/`, scoped under the `.lagoon` root class). Studio's app UI (dashboard, Tables, SQL editor, settings) is still the earlier light shadcn look and is **not** part of this system yet. Per PRODUCT.md, the dark default and the pastel colour roles are meant to be inherited by later Studio work; the chart furniture vocabulary is the landing's expression and should be adapted, not pasted, when app screens adopt the world. The Spectral "Chelabase" wordmark is provisional; no logo, favicon or brand mark exists. All imagery is code-drawn SVG and CSS; no raster assets ship.

Density is calm and editorial at the page level, precise at the instrument level: generous section gaps, measured line lengths, and hairline rules doing the structural work that shadows and fills do elsewhere.
keyCharacteristics: Dark by default: lagoon ink ground with teal in it, never slate or neutral black.
Pastel roles, each with a fixed meaning: sand acts, seafoam is water and "yes", coral is hazard and "not yet", palm is land.
Structure from hairlines: single and double rules, graduated tick borders, dashed survey lines.
Serif for the chart's voice (names, headings, italic annotations), a hyperlegible sans for reading, mono only for code.
Motion is survey motion: lines draw once, ripples mark a restore, the focused legend row lifts while others recede.

rules.name: The One Meaning Per Pastel Rule
rules.body: Sand is action, seafoam is water and yes, coral is hazard and not-yet, palm is land. A pastel is never used decoratively against its meaning; a coral button or a sand error is wrong.

rules.name: The Fields Own Regions Rule
rules.body: Pastels appear as whole depth bands or as engraved line colour, not as tinted cards. A pastel field is set in lagoon ink, with its own selection and focus colours flipped to ink.

rules.name: The Lagoon Not Slate Rule
rules.body: Every dark surface carries teal (hue around 200-210). Neutral greys and blue-slates are off-world.

rules.name: The Italic Is Lettering Rule
rules.body: Spectral italic is the chart's annotation voice: names on the water, soundings, notes on the drawing, captions. It is not used for emphasis in running text.

rules.name: The Serif Speaks, Sans Reads Rule
rules.body: Headings and chart lettering are Spectral; anything a visitor reads at length or clicks is Atkinson. No uppercase-tracked label styles.

rules.name: The Hairline Before Shadow Rule
rules.body: Separation comes from 1px rules at 16% or 34% chalk. Shadows are reserved for the cartouche and the primary plate's hover; everything else is flat.

rules.name: The Double Rule Rule
rules.body: Framed objects (cartouche, key, plates, neat-line frame) carry an outer rule and an inner rule inset 3-8px. The inner rule is what makes them chart furniture.

dos: **Do** keep the ground lagoon ink and let pastels own whole regions or engraved lines, each in its one role (sand acts, seafoam is water and yes, coral is hazard and not-yet, palm is land).
**Do** build controls as chart furniture: plates with a 2px outer and 1px inner rule, neat-line tabs, the tide staff.
**Do** separate with 1px hairlines at 16% or 34% chalk, and give framed objects a second inner rule.
**Do** set headings and chart lettering in Spectral (italic for annotations) and reading text in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next.
**Do** use dashed lines for provisional, planned or surveyed-not-built things, and solid lines for what exists.
**Do** draw every image in SVG or CSS and label synthetic drawings as illustrations.
**Do** flip selection and focus colours to ink on pastel fields, and keep focus a 2px sand outline elsewhere.
**Do** honour reduced motion with static final states and no ripples.
donts: **Don't** use neon glow, purple SaaS gradients, or cream-and-terracotta editorial palettes.
**Don't** use neutral greys or blue-slate darks; every dark carries lagoon teal.
**Don't** use stock shadcn buttons, pill buttons, or a feature-card grid on this world's surfaces.
**Don't** build a split hero with a glowing git graph; branching is drawn as surveyed channels on the chart.
**Don't** use uppercase-tracked eyebrow or kicker labels above headings.
**Don't** add drop shadows beyond the cartouche settle and the primary plate's hover glow.
**Don't** use clip-art coastal imagery; palms and the crab appear as small engraved chart symbols, sparingly.
**Don't** treat the provisional wordmark as a logo or derive marks from it.
